import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1072

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1072](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1072)
-/

open Nat Filter Finset Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1072

/-- For any prime $p$, let $f(p)$ be the least integer such that $f(p)! + 1 \equiv 0 \mod p$. -/
noncomputable def f (p : ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {n | (n)! + 1 ≡ 0 [MOD p]}

/-- Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p) = p − 1$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that $f(p)/p \to 0$ for $p \to \infty$ in a density 1 subset of the primes? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (P : Set ℕ), P ⊆ {p | p.Prime} ∧ P.HasDensity 1 {p | p.Prime} ∧
      Tendsto (fun p => (f p / p : ℝ)) (atTop ⊓ principal P) (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry
/--
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02], believed that the number of $p \le x$ for which $f(p)=p−1$
is $o(x/\log x)$.

[HaSu02] Hardy, G. E. and Subbarao, M. V., _A modified problem of Pillai and some related questions._
Amer. Math. Monthly (2002), 554--559.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1072.variants.littleo :
    (fun x ↦ (({p | p.Prime ∧ f p = p - 1} ∩ Icc 0 x).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x ↦ x / Real.log x) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1072

reformulations.difference: The minimum permits n = 0, giving f 2 = 0. The associated OEIS records A073944 and A154554 use the positive-index convention, giving f(2) = 1 and including 2 among primes with f(p) = p − 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every prime p ≠ 2, a solution n = 0 would imply p divides 2, so the two minima agree. Their sets of primes satisfying f(p) = p − 1 therefore differ exactly by inserting 2, preserving infinitude. The ratios agree eventually along every subset of primes, preserving the density-one limit statement. For cutoffs x ≥ 2 the counting functions differ by 1, and 1 = o(x/log x), preserving the little-o variant. All three corresponding equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Thus this convention difference is harmless, not a misformalization.

review.notes: Source-limited review, not a complete certification of faithfulness. The cited Erdős webpage and Hardy–Subbarao full text returned access challenges. The accessible Erdős database records problem 1072 as open, consistent with the file, but does not separately establish the variant's status. Local checks passed: Wilson guarantees a nonempty defining set at every prime; division is real-valued; density is relative to primes; density one forces P to be infinite and the restricted filter non-bottom; all counted sets are finite; logarithm/division defaults at small cutoffs are irrelevant atTop. The scratch file compiles without errors, and the reviewed file was not modified.
